newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 5.5/6.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 5.5/6.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 5.5/6.0 percent on Friday morning on sustained ample supply.
Dealers said carry-forward liquidity and central bank supply of 359 billion rupiah continued to keep the market flush.
"There is not much room for arbitrage despite the ample supply. We are still worried about possible (future) tightening," one said.
"We are already long at present. The focus is still on tax payments," a Japanese bank dealer said.
One state bank dealer said the flush market which kept the returns on rupiah less attractive and the absence of longer term central bank papers seemed to have reduced foreign inflows.
"But foreign investors appear to have switched to other alternatives, including bonds and mutual funds. We feel there are still foreign funds in the market," she said.
One- and three-month money were at 10.75/11.00 and 12.75/13.00 percent, respectively.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates stable. It offered seven-day SBIs at 6.5 percent, 14-day at 8.5 percent and one-month at 10.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 5.83 percent, compared with 8.25 percent on Wednesday.
Bond dealers said the market remained buoyant following the mushrooming of fresh mutual funds which placed the majority of their funds in fixed income papers, including bonds.
The yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was at around 15.0 percent on a price of 107.25 percent.
